nodes.name: NF pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A piece of NF (2 cm×4 cm) was first ultrasonically washed in a 6 M HCl solution for 15 min in order to remove the NiOx surface layers, and then rinsed with ethanol, acetone, and deionized (DI) water in sequence for several times.
nodes.source_text: a piece of NF (2 cm×4 cm) was first ultrasonically washed in a 6 M HCl solution for 15 min... rinsed with ethanol, acetone, and deionized (DI) water in sequence for several times.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 349 mg of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 161 mg of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and 120 mg of urea were subjected to a mixed solution of DI water (10 mL) and ethylene glycol (30 mL), which was then stirred for 30 min to totally dissolve. The solutions together with the acid-washed NF were subjected to a 100 mL stainless-steel Teflon-lined autoclave, sealed, and maintained in an oven at 120°C for 12 h. After cooling down, the sample (NiFe-LDH@NF) was taken out, washed with DI water and absolute ethanol several times, and then dried in an oven at 80°C overnight.

nodes.name: NiFeRh-LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: For the preparation of NiFeRh-LDH on NF, the procedure is the same as NiFe-LDH except the additional added RhCl3·xH2O (different dosages: 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, and 0.3 mmol corresponding to samples 1-6) during the hydrothermal process. NiFeRh-LDH with a Rh content of 0.99 at.% was used for material characterizations.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Same as NiFe-LDH procedure but with additional RhCl3·xH2O (0.025-0.3 mmol) added to tailor Rh contents

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 11.4°, 22.97°, 34.43°, 38.99°, 59.94°, and 61.26° index to (003), (006), (012), (015), (110), and (113) planes of NiFe-LDH. After Rh doping, (003) reflection shifts negatively by 0.2° indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Peaks at 11.4°, 22.97°, 34.43°, 38.99°, 59.94°, and 61.26° were discerned (Fig. 2a), indexing to (003), (006), (012), (015), (110) and (113) planes of NiFe-LDH ... (003) reflection in the XRD patterns of NiFeRh-LDH is shifted negatively by 0.2°

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeRh-LDH survey shows faint Rh peak confirming doping. Ni 2p at 855.81/873.58 eV (Ni²⁺), Fe 2p at 710.68/724.25 eV (Fe³⁺), Rh 3d at 308.83/313.65 eV (Rh³⁺) and 307/312.02 eV (Rh⁰). All Ni/Fe peaks negatively shift vs NiFe-LDH. O 1s shows stronger peak at 531.5 eV indicating more oxygen vacancies in NiFeRh-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to NiFe-LDH, an additional faint Rh peak is found in the survey spectra of NiFeRh-LDH ... The peak center at 531.5 eV of NiFeRh-LDH is significantly stronger than the counterpart of NiFe-LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeRh-LDH shows interconnected nanosheets vertically grown on NF with larger sheet size than NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: interconnected NiFe-LDH nanosheets were vertically grow on NF ... After introduction of Rh, similar interconnected nanosheets were observed in NiFeRh-LDH ... the size of the sheet is larger than that of NiFe-LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeRh-LDH nanosheets have ultrathin feature with thickness ~1.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The thickness of nanosheet was measured to be ~1.5 nm at one edge of the nanosheet (Fig. 3d)

nodes.characterization_summary: Well-resolved lattice fringe of 0.24 nm indexed to (015) plane of NiFeRh-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the well-resolved lattice fringe was measured to be 0.24 nm, which can be indexed to the (015) plane of NiFeRh-LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: Concentric rings assigned to (015) and (110) planes of NiFeRh-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the captured selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 3f), the concentric rings ... being assigned to (015) and (110) planes of NiFeRh-LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: No particles or impurities discerned in NiFeRh-LDH, confirming homogeneous Rh doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: we also captured the high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images of NiFeRh-LDH ... no any particles or impurities were discerned

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni, Fe, Rh, and O elements uniformly distributed over NiFeRh-LDH nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image and the corresponding EDX elemental mapping were captured as well (Figs. 3g and S14), which present that Ni, Fe, Rh and O elements are uniformly distributed

nodes.characterization_summary: d-band center of NiFeRh-LDH at -5.31 eV, positively shifted from -5.2 eV of NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the d-band centers of NiFeRh-LDH and NiFe-LDH can be verified to be -5.31 and -5.2 eV, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Used to determine elemental composition including Rh content of 0.99 at.% in NiFeRh-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS, EDS and ICP-OES were involved to determine the contents of Rh in the as-prepared samples. NiFeRh-LDH with a Rh content of 0.99 at.%

nodes.characterization_summary: Strong signal at g=2.002 confirms oxygen vacancies in NiFeRh-LDH; signal at g=4.29 for Fe clusters; g=2.09 stronger in NiFeRh-LDH indicating electronic modulation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to NiFe-LDH, a strong signal at g = 2.002 was observed in NiFeRh-LDH ... informing the existence of oxygen vacancies in NiFeRh-LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDS and STEM-EDS mapping confirm uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Rh, O over NiFeRh-LDH nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM-EDS mapping of NiFeRh-LDH was also collected, which demonstrates that Ni, Fe, Rh, and O are uniformly distributed over the whole nanosheets
